items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Just have Ray Nance do it. Same tune.

ctx.x: Yeah. He had a name for everybody. He wrote for individual players. That way they kept a good span for – never wrote anything too high for Ray Nance. All the high notes are done by Cat Anderson. So it is personalized. I learned to do that. It saves a lot. I still do that today. In fact I’m getting a score sent in from L.A., a thing called Opus No.6. I’ll been rehearsing with a band Monday. That’s a full band. I gave the copyist a full sketch. He learned from that. I did that a couple weeks ago. If I didn’t have a…
Use that shorthand that Duke Ellington – now, what about Strayhorn? How did he prepare his? Did he use the same method?
